CheckTitle: Bitbucket workspaces have no inactive administrator accounts
Description: Workspace members holding the `owner` permission can change access controls, delete repositories and manage every pipeline. This check reports owner accounts whose Atlassian account status is not active, which indicates a deactivated or unverified identity still holding administrative rights.
Risk: An inactive account retaining owner permission is an **orphaned administrative path**: nobody monitors it, its password may never be rotated, and reactivating it — through account recovery or an IdP mistake — silently restores full workspace control. Offboarding processes that only disable the identity provider entry frequently leave this Bitbucket-side grant in place.

Code.Other:
1. Open the workspace in Bitbucket
2. Go to **Settings > User groups** and the workspace members list
3. Review every member holding **Admin**
4. Remove members whose Atlassian account is inactive or no longer employed
5. Reduce remaining owners to the minimum, and record who is expected to hold the role
6. Add a recurring access review so the list is re-confirmed each quarter

Recommendation.Text: Remove workspace admin permission from inactive accounts, keep the owner set as small as practical, and review it on a recurring schedule tied to your joiner-mover-leaver process.
